rules: Only URLs seen in search results are listed; none opened or verified.
Internal classification is not a legal determination.
coverage_gaps: Turkey (JUR-0091): Law 7258 (state monopoly on sports betting and games of chance: Spor Toto, Milli Piyango, Jockey Club); Penal Code Art. 228 and Law 5651 cover illegal gambling and site blocking (law-firm sources). Only the Spor Toto page above was seen.
Japan (JUR-0011): Penal Code Arts. 185-186; online casinos illegal even if licensed abroad; 2025 measures against promoting online gambling (DLA Piper, trade press). No e-Gov or NPA URL seen.

Thailand (JUR-0069): Gambling Act B.E. 2478 (1935); Computer Crime Act s.20 blocking; draft amendment to allow authorised online gambling under consultation in 2026 (Tilleke & Gibbins). No Royal Gazette or Council of State URL seen.

Vietnam (JUR-0090): casinos licensed by Ministry of Finance; locals allowed only in a pilot (Resolution 8/2025/NQ-CP); online betting illegal for citizens; Decree 121/2021 covers foreigner-only electronic games. Only commercial legal databases (thuvienphapluat.vn, hethongphapluat.vn) surfaced, not listed as sources.

Hong Kong (JUR-0016): Gambling Ordinance Cap. 148 and Betting Duty Ordinance Cap. 108; HKJC is the only authorised operator; offshore betting made illegal in 2002 amendment. Only old LegCo papers seen; elegislation.gov.hk URL not seen.

Taiwan (JUR-0095): Criminal Code Art. 266 amended Jan 2022 to cover online gambling; Sports Lottery Issuance Act amended 2025; state sports lottery is the only legal betting. No usable law.moj.gov.tw URL confirmed (the one seen carried a constitution code).
Pakistan: Prevention of Gambling Act 1977 (based on Public Gambling Act 1867); a National Assembly PDF is cited but no URL seen.
Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain: prohibited on religious/legal grounds; only generic commentary found; no official URLs.

Not yet searched individually: Brunei, Jordan, Mauritania, Bangladesh, China, Laos, Lebanon, Algeria, Tunisia, Egypt, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Tonga, plus the 13 unclear and 17 sanctions-driven jurisdictions.

sources.notes: Betting Act 1953 (Act 495). URL seen as a link on a Wikipedia page, not opened. Common Gaming Houses Act 1953 (Act 289) URL not seen. 2026 reform of both Acts and a Cyber Crime Bill reported by trade press only.
